part1.label: Part 1
part1.title: Familiar topics
part1.tip: Answer naturally. Add a reason or a short example.

topics.title: Your hometown
topics.prompt: What do you like most about the place where you live?
points: Has your hometown changed in recent years?
Would you like to live there in the future?
Where would you take someone who was visiting for the first time?
Is there anything you wish your hometown had?

topics.title: Your daily routine
topics.prompt: What do you usually do in the morning?
points: What is your favourite time of day?
Is your routine different on weekends?
Would you like to change anything about your routine?
Do you prefer to plan your day in advance?

topics.title: Learning English
topics.prompt: When did you start learning English?
points: What do you enjoy about learning it?
How do you practise outside class?
Which part of learning English do you find most difficult?
When was the last time you used English outside a lesson?

topics.title: Food and cooking
topics.prompt: Do you enjoy cooking?
points: What kind of food do you usually eat at home?
Did you learn to cook when you were younger?
Is there a dish you would like to learn to make?
Do you prefer cooking alone or with someone else?

topics.title: Public transport
topics.prompt: How often do you use public transport?
points: What kind of transport do you use most often?
What do you like or dislike about it?
How could transport in your area be improved?
What do you usually do while waiting for a bus or train?

topics.title: Photography
topics.prompt: What do you usually take photos of?
points: Do you prefer taking photos or being in them?
How often do you look at old photos?
Do you prefer keeping photos on your phone or printing them?
When do you decide to share a photo with someone?

topics.title: Quiet places
topics.prompt: Where do you go when you want some peace and quiet?
points: How often do you spend time there?
What do you usually do in a quiet place?
Did you enjoy quiet places when you were younger?
Do you concentrate better in silence or with some background sound?

topics.title: Learning from others
topics.prompt: Who do you usually ask when you want to learn how to do something?
points: Do you prefer someone to show you an example or explain the steps?
What is something a friend has taught you?
Have you ever taught someone a skill?
Is there anything you prefer learning by yourself?

topics.title: Borrowing and lending
topics.prompt: Do you often borrow things from friends or family?
points: What kinds of things are you happy to lend to others?
How do you remember to return something you have borrowed?
Did you share toys or books when you were a child?
Is there anything you would rather buy than borrow?

topics.title: Shopping locally
topics.prompt: What do you usually buy from shops near your home?
points: Is there a local shop you visit regularly?
Do you prefer shopping at a busy time or a quiet time?
Has where you shop changed in recent years?
Do you enjoy talking to people who work in local shops?

topics.title: Changing plans
topics.prompt: Do you usually make plans for your free time?
points: How do you feel when a plan changes at the last minute?
What do you do when rainy weather changes your plans?
Do you prefer making plans alone or with friends?
Have you ever enjoyed a day more because you had no plan?

topics.title: Useful objects
topics.prompt: What small object do you use almost every day?
points: When did you start using it?
Where do you usually keep it?
Would you replace it with the same thing if you lost it?
Is there an object you use less often now than in the past?

part2.label: Part 2
part2.title: Long turn
part2.tip: Take one minute to plan. Try speaking for one to two minutes.

topics.title: A place you enjoy visiting
topics.prompt: Describe a place you enjoy visiting in your free time.
points: Say where the place is.
Say when you usually go there.
Describe what you do there.
Explain why you enjoy visiting this place.

topics.title: A skill you would like to learn
topics.prompt: Describe a skill you would like to learn in the future.
points: Say what the skill is.
Explain why you want to learn it.
Describe how you would learn it.
Explain how this skill could help you.

topics.title: Someone who helped you
topics.prompt: Describe a person who helped you during a difficult time.
points: Say who the person is.
Describe the situation.
Explain how the person helped you.
Say how you felt afterwards.

topics.title: A meal you remember
topics.prompt: Describe a meal you had that you still remember.
points: Say when and where you had the meal.
Say who you ate with.
Describe what you ate.
Explain why you still remember the meal.

topics.title: A journey that did not go as planned
topics.prompt: Describe a journey that did not go as planned.
points: Say where you were going.
Explain how you planned to get there.
Describe what went wrong and what you did.
Explain what you would do differently next time.

topics.title: A photograph that matters to you
topics.prompt: Describe a photograph that is important to you.
points: Describe what the photograph shows.
Say when and where it was taken.
Explain how you got the photograph.
Say why it is important to you.

topics.title: A quiet place you discovered
topics.prompt: Describe a quiet place you found unexpectedly.
points: Say where the place is.
Explain how you found it.
Describe what you noticed when you arrived.
Explain whether you would visit it again.

topics.title: A useful piece of advice
topics.prompt: Describe a piece of advice that changed how you did something.
points: Say who gave you the advice.
Explain what you were trying to do.
Describe how you used the advice.
Explain why you would or would not pass it on.

topics.title: Something you borrowed
topics.prompt: Describe something you borrowed that helped you complete a task.
points: Say what you borrowed.
Explain who lent it to you.
Describe how you used it.
Explain what you would have done without it.

topics.title: A shop you would recommend
topics.prompt: Describe a local shop you would recommend to someone.
points: Say where the shop is.
Describe what it sells.
Explain what happened on one of your visits.
Say who you would recommend it to and why.

topics.title: A plan you changed for the better
topics.prompt: Describe a time when changing your plans led to a better result.
points: Say what you originally planned.
Explain why you decided to change it.
Describe what you did instead.
Explain what you learned from the experience.

topics.title: Something you repaired
topics.prompt: Describe an object you repaired or helped someone repair.
points: Say what the object was.
Explain what went wrong with it.
Describe what you or someone else did to fix it.
Explain why you decided to repair it.

part3.label: Part 3
part3.title: Discussion
part3.tip: Explain your views and support them with reasons or examples.

topics.title: Cities and communities
topics.prompt: What makes a neighbourhood a good place to live?
points: Why do many people move to cities?
What public spaces help people get to know their neighbours?
How can cities make public spaces accessible to everyone?

topics.title: Technology and learning
topics.prompt: How has technology changed the way people learn new skills?
points: Which skills are difficult to learn entirely online?
How can adults make time to learn while working?
What can a teacher offer that a video lesson cannot?

topics.title: Work and personal time
topics.prompt: How much responsibility should employers have for workers’ personal well-being?
points: Why do some people work very long hours?
How can employers help workers balance their jobs and personal lives?
Do flexible hours benefit all workers equally?

topics.title: Food and traditions
topics.prompt: Why are certain meals important to a community's identity?
points: How have family eating habits changed over time?
Why do some traditional dishes become less common?
What can schools or communities do to keep local food traditions alive?

topics.title: Transport and travel
topics.prompt: What makes people choose a private vehicle over public transport?
points: Should cities spend more on public transport or on roads?
How can towns with fewer passengers provide reliable transport?
How might travel habits change in the future?

topics.title: Photographs and memories
topics.prompt: How has smartphone photography changed the way people remember events?
points: Why might people remember an event differently after seeing photos of it?
What should people consider before sharing photos of others online?
How can photographs help younger generations understand the past?

topics.title: Quiet spaces in public life
topics.prompt: Why might people need quiet spaces in busy towns and cities?
points: How can libraries serve people who want silence and people who want to work together?
Should parks include areas where organised activities are limited?
How could town planners make quiet spaces available to people in crowded neighbourhoods?

topics.title: Advice and decision-making
topics.prompt: Why do people sometimes ignore good advice?
points: When is advice from someone with a similar experience especially helpful?
How can young people decide which advice online to trust?
Should schools teach students how to ask for and respond to advice?

topics.title: Sharing instead of buying
topics.prompt: When does borrowing something make more sense than owning it?
points: Why might neighbours hesitate to share tools or equipment?
What rules would help a community lending service work well?
Could borrowing become more common if people had less space at home?

topics.title: Local shops and online shopping
topics.prompt: What can small shops offer that large online stores cannot?
points: Why do some people still prefer to shop in person even when prices are higher?
How can small businesses use online services without losing their local identity?
What happens to a neighbourhood when many of its shops close?

topics.title: Planning and adaptability
topics.prompt: Why do some people cope better with unexpected changes than others?
points: When can a detailed plan make it harder to respond to a change?
How can group projects teach students to adapt when plans go wrong?
Should organisations reward people for sticking to a plan or for finding a better approach?

topics.title: Repairing and replacing
topics.prompt: Why do people sometimes replace items that could still be repaired?
points: Should manufacturers make spare parts available for longer?
What could encourage people to learn basic repair skills?
Who should pay when an item is difficult to repair because of the way it was designed?
